subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Model Mix in Practice
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Model Mix in Practice.

hook.text: No real company uses just one service model. Modern stacks mix IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and serverless together.

buildup.text: The database might be managed PaaS. The frontend deploys on serverless. The ML pipeline runs on IaaS VMs.

discovery.text: Choosing the right model per component — not per company — is how experienced teams architect systems.

twist.text: The mix evolves over time. Teams often start with PaaS, then move critical parts to IaaS for control.

climax.text: There's no perfect architecture. There's only the right architecture for your team, today.

punchline.text: Mix models per problem. There's no one-size-fits-all cloud.

quiz.question: How do experienced teams choose cloud service models?
options: They pick the best model for each individual component, not one model for everything
They always use the cheapest model for all components
They use only one model to keep the architecture simple

details.summary: Real-world cloud architectures almost always combine IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and serverless within the same organization. A typical setup might use IaaS for legacy apps, PaaS for web services, SaaS for business tools, and serverless for event processing.
details.whyItMatters: Forcing all workloads into a single model wastes resources or limits capabilities. Matching each workload to its optimal model maximizes efficiency and developer productivity.
takeaways: Most organizations use a mix of IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and serverless
Each workload should be matched to its optimal service model
The mix evolves as applications are modernized over time

faq.question: How do you decide which model for each workload?
faq.answer: Evaluate each workload's need for control, its operational complexity tolerance, team expertise, compliance requirements, and scaling patterns. Legacy apps often start on IaaS and migrate to PaaS or serverless as they are modernized over time.

faq.question: Do service model choices affect cost?
faq.answer: Significantly. IaaS costs more to operate due to management overhead. PaaS charges a premium for automation. SaaS pricing scales with users. Serverless can be cheapest for sporadic workloads but expensive for sustained high-throughput. Total cost must include people, not just infrastructure.
